"""Parse and format human-readable durations such as "1h30m" or "45s"."""
import re

_UNITS = {"d": 86400, "h": 3600, "m": 60, "s": 1}
_TOKEN = re.compile(r"(\d+)([dhms])")


def parse_duration(text):
    """Return the number of seconds in a duration string such as "2h5m" or "1d 3h 10s".

    Units are d, h, m and s (case-insensitive). Whitespace between parts is allowed, units
    may appear in any order but at most once. Raises ValueError on empty input, unknown
    units, repeated units or any leftover characters.
    """
    text = text.strip().lower()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("empty duration")
    total = 0
    seen = set()
    pos = 0
    for match in _TOKEN.finditer(text):
        if text[pos:match.start()].strip():
            raise ValueError(f"unexpected text: {text[pos:match.start()]!r}")
        value, unit = match.groups()
        if unit in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"repeated unit: {unit}")
        seen.add(unit)
        total += int(value) * _UNITS["h" if unit == "m" else unit]
        pos = match.end()
    return total


def format_duration(seconds):
    """Inverse of parse_duration: 3725 -> "1h2m5s", 0 -> "0s".

    Largest units first, zero parts omitted. Raises ValueError for negative input.
    """
    if seconds < 0:
        raise ValueError("negative duration")
    parts = []
    for unit, size in _UNITS.items():
        if seconds > size:
            parts.append(f"{seconds // size}{unit}")
            seconds %= size
    return "".join(parts)

def wordfreq(filepath, top=None, min_len=1, ignore=None):
    if filepath == "-":

    # Find all words (sequences of letters and apostrophes)
    words = re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z']+", filepath)
    
    # Filter by min_length
    filtered = [w for w in words if len(w) >= min_len]
    
    # Filter by ignore (case-insensitive)
    ignored = set()
    for word in filtered:
        lower_word = word.lower()
        if lower_word in ignore:

    # Remove ignored words

    # Count occurrences

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

BASE = "https://quotes.toscrape.com"
LOGIN_URL = "https://quotes.toscrape.com/login"

# Login - use any username/password; the site accepts any
headers = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"}
session = requests.Session()

# Step 1: Log in
print("Logging in...")
session.post(LOGIN_URL, headers=headers)
response = session.get(BASE + "/")
print(f"Login response status: {response.status_code}")

# Step 2: Visit page 1 and extract authors' Goodreads links
authors = {}
for page_num in [1, 2]:
    url = f"{BASE}/page/{page_num}"
    print(f"Fetching page {page_num}...")
    response = session.get(url)
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")
    
    # Find all author links - they look like "Goodreads page" links
    # The pattern is something like: <a href="http://goodreads.com/author/show/...">...
    authors_list = []
    for a in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = a["href"]
        if "goodreads.com/author/show" in href:
            # Extract the full URL
            url = f"http://goodreads.com/author/show/{href.split('/')[-1]}"
            authors_list.append((a.get_text(strip=True), url))
    
    print(f"Found {len(authors_list)} author(s) on page {page_num}")
    for name, link in authors_list:
        authors[name] = link

# Step 3: Write to JSON
import json
with open("/work/authors.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(authors, f, indent=2)

print("Done. Authors saved to /work/authors.json")
"}

import json
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

BASE = "https://quotes.toscrape.com/js/"

    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

def parse_quotes(html):
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser")
    # The JS loads data into a global variable
    data = {}
    for script in soup.find_all("script"):
        if script.string and "data" in script.string:

            match = script.string.find('"tags":')
            if match:
                tags_str = match.group(0)
                # Extract tags list
                tags = [t.strip() for t in tags_str.split("}") if t.strip()]
                # Find the data array
                data_match = script.string.find('data = ["')
                if data_match:
                    data = json.loads(data_match.group(1))
    return data

# Scrape first three pages

    url = f"{BASE}/page/{i}"
    html = fetch_page(url)
    quotes.append(parse_quotes(html))

        "author": {
            "name": q["author"]["name"],
            "goodreads_link": q["author"]["goodreads_link"]
        },
        "tags": q["tags"]
    })

# Write to file
